summary: HR Phase 3 (Manpower Planning · Deployment · Mobilization · Demobilization · Replacement · Rollups) — full backend + frontend integration tested. 25/25 pytest PASS against public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Frontend hub at /app/hr/manpower-planning was missing its <Route> in App.js (HrPhase3 component imported but never wired) — fixed during test run. Also fixed a syntax error at the end of App.js (stray '/BrowserRouter>' block) that was breaking the entire frontend build. After both fixes the hub loads, all 9 tabs render, CRUD on Requirements works against backend, and Mobilization/Demobilization/Replacement/Availability/Calendar/Dashboard tabs all render and respond to clicks. Existing /api/hr (leave), /api/hr1 (phase1) and /api/hr2 (phase2) endpoints untouched — no regression.

minor.issue: test function test_deployment_full_flow has `return dep` which pytest warns about (PytestReturnNotNoneWarning). Cosmetic — replace with assert or remove the return.

ui_bugs.issue: Stray '/BrowserRouter>... </ThemeProvider> );}' block at the end of file caused 'Unterminated regular expression' SyntaxError and broke the entire frontend webpack build. FIXED by testing agent.

Route for /app/hr/manpower-planning was missing — HrPhase3 imported but never mounted. Layout sidebar nav-hr-manpower pointed to a dead URL. FIXED by testing agent (added <Route path="/app/hr/manpower-planning" element={...HrPhase3.../>).

allow_multi_site override is a shadcn Select (Yes/No) without a data-testid on its trigger. Spec said `data-testid dep-allow_multi_site` should exist on the toggle but it currently exists only on the checkboxes for accommodation/travel/ppe/tool. Recommend adding data-testid='dep-allow_multi_site' to the SelectTrigger at HrPhase3.jsx:351.

action_items: (Optional) Add data-testid='dep-allow_multi_site' to the allow_multi_site SelectTrigger in /app/frontend/src/pages/hr/HrPhase3.jsx so playbook spec matches.
(Optional) Replace `return dep` with assertions in test_deployment_full_flow to silence the pytest warning.
Main agent should verify that the App.js route fix and trash-block removal are kept in subsequent edits (these were live during this test run).
critical_code_review_comments: App.js had a syntax-breaking trailing block — main agent should verify file integrity after every multi-file write.
HrPhase3 route wiring was forgotten — recommend adding a smoke test that visits the new route after creating a hub page so dead-link issues fail fast.

_recompute_requirement_availability uses regex with raw user-supplied skill — special-character skills (e.g. 'C/C++') could be a partial ReDoS or regex compile-time failure. Recommend re.escape() before $regex.
availability_by_skill iterates per-person doing async _compliance_status, which calls today_d/now twice per person — for very large pools this is N+1-like; consider vectorizing.

Active-deployment guard checks `employee_id` but `_resolve_person` accepts `person_id` for workers too — code is correct but variable naming is mixed; recommend renaming to `person_id` consistently in `deployments` collection.

success_rate.frontend: 95% (all 9 tabs, requirement create, allow_multi_site present as Select but missing data-testid)

seed_data_creation: Pytest run created several PRJ-PYT-* manpower requirements, deployments (DEP-2026-####), MOB-2026-####, DMB-2026-####, REP-2026-####. UI run created an additional 'PRJ-UI-HR3' requirement.
context_for_next_testing_agent: HR Phase 3 backend + frontend both green. App.js had 2 issues now fixed (stray trailing block, missing manpower-planning route). Next phase work won't need to redo any of this. dep-allow_multi_site data-testid is the only remaining cosmetic miss.
rca of the issue: App.js compile error: a previous merge appended a duplicated tail of the file ('/BrowserRouter>... }') after the closing brace, producing an Unterminated regex SyntaxError during babel parse. Removed lines 251-255. Missing route: the HrPhase3 component was imported at line 93 and a sidebar nav link existed in Layout.jsx pointing to /app/hr/manpower-planning, but no <Route path='/app/hr/manpower-planning'> existed in App.js, so visiting the URL fell through to the wildcard route and redirected to home. Added the route adjacent to /app/hr/operations.
